text:
Ava M: Quick idea — build a tiny "access-orch" that sits in front of our query pools. Responsibilities: compute per-dashboard visibility, emit a compact signed visibility blob, and return downscoped fetch tokens for each tile group. Keeps routing and policy logic out of UI and query nodes.

Diego R: How's this different from the earlier "orchestrator" chat? Need concrete perf and safety constraints.

Ava M: Differs in two ways: 1) tokens are lightweight JWT-like blobs (base64 + HMAC) with a visibility bitmap instead of full ACLs; 2) cache-first policy evaluation with LRU per-tenant entries and TTLs tuned to org config churn. Goal: <2ms warm added latency.

Nina P: Token format? We need to guarantee no escalation if token leaked. TTL? revocation?

Ava M: Draft token shape: rw-dscope-v1|tenant:123|exp:1670000000|vis:AAE3|sig:... Vis is a hex bitmap of allowed tiles. TTL default 30s for interactive tiles, 5m for background jobs. Revocation via short TTL + a blacklist service for immediate kill (rare).

Tom H: Bitmap size might grow for big dashboards. Suggest compressing runs and using a tile-grouping id to reduce bitmap width. Also, we should support a "full-access" marker for legacy orgs.

Ravi V: Ops concerns: single service == single failure blast radius. Plan for high-availability? autoscale, multi-AZ, and a hard fallback path where UI asks query layer directly with the session token (no downscope). That fallback should be O(1) and fast.

Ava M: Exactly. Fallback flow: if access-orch times out, UI sends original session token + header X-RW-ORCH:skipped and query layer does local check. We log a metric "access_orch.fallback_count".

Diego R: Caching details? How do we maintain consistency when org permissions change?

Ava M: Cache keys: tenant_id + dashboard_hash + user_roles. TTL configurable per org, default 15s. On org policy change we bump a config-store version which becomes part of cache key; propagates invalidation without immediate cache eviction.

Nina P: Auditability: how do we trace which actor requested a tile and which policy allowed it? Need trace headers and audit events.

Ava M: Access-orch will propagate trace id and add header X-RW-ACCESS: "dscope=v1;vis_sha=abcd;src=access-orch". Also emit an audit event (tenant, user, dashboard, tiles, decision) to event-store; sample 100% for canary tenants, 1% for others.

Tom H: Security: signing key rotation is important. Use KMS-backed keys with key-id in token (kid) and a graceful rotation window where both old and new keys validate for 10 minutes.

Ravi V: Rollout suggestion: 1) run access-orch as read-only simulator for 72h (service returns decision but UI ignores it), 2) enable per-tenant opt-in with 1% traffic, 3) raise to 25% with health guards, 4) 100% after 2 weeks no regressions.

Diego R: Metrics we need: access_orch.lat_ms (p50/p95/p99), tile_visibility_cache_hit, token_sign_latency, token_verify_latency, fallback_rate, audit_event_rate. Add alerts for p99>50ms or fallback_rate>0.5% sustained.

Nina P: For legality/compliance: persist audit events for 1 year; ensure visibility bitmap does not leak PHI. If a tile contains sensitive attributes we mark tile-group as "sensitive" and orchestrator will not return downscoped tokens for external integrations.

Ava M: Implementation notes: small Go service, vettable policy evaluator compiled from role->bitmask rules (no dynamic SQL in hot path). Expose two endpoints: /decide (sync) and /decide-batch (batch dashboard tiles). Return schema: {decision_version, token, visibility_root_hash}.

Tom H: Query layer needs to validate tokens quickly — HMAC verify + small table lookup for tile-group metadata. I'll prototype verify path and microbench it.

ci-bot: Repo created: infra/access-orch (starter CI + helm chart).

Ravi V: Action items: Ava to write RFC + token spec, Tom to bench verify path, Diego to add perf guard thresholds to SLOs, Nina to draft audit retention & compliance notes. Sync Friday 9:30am. :white_check_mark:
